The distributions of these options reflect 2023 saturation levels of EV technology and operation in the United States, ensuring that EV-related measures capture expected diversity3. All dwelling units are sampled with percentage of vehicle charge at home, a vehicle type, and a VMT. These options are only relevant in the baseline for dwelling units with an EV but are used to define vehicle and driving characteristics for dwelling units that adopt an EV in this measure. Table 1 describes the ResStock characteristics, or dependencies, that influence the distribution of EV-related options. Figure 2 illustrates how these dependencies shape the baseline distributions for “EV Ownership,” highlighting the significant variation that can occur across regions, housing characteristics, and demographics. California has a relatively high rate of EV adoption and diversity in housing characteristics and demographics, which makes underlying trends easier to observe and interpret. The ResStock input files are distributions of parameters assigned in the baseline simulation but also represent parameters that can be adjusted in a measure. ResStock leverages the OpenStudio-HPXML workflow to model individual dwelling units as OpenStudio® models, with each ResStock option assigned one or more arguments in OpenStudio-HPXML to directly inform the energy model inputs. 7 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
